name: Lace-Fragment
geological_features: Interconnected void spaces throughout the body
Surface covered in delicate mineral formations
specific_features: Rock so porous it appears lace-like in cross-section
Internal cavities large enough to house structures
description: Lace-Fragment is a tiny rocky body with an internal structure unlike any other known world. The rock is extraordinarily porous, riddled with interconnected void spaces that give it a lace-like appearance when viewed in cross-section. This porosity was created during the body's formation, when volcanic outgassing created bubbles in the cooling rock that linked together before solidifying, producing a natural foam structure on a planetary scale. The surface gravity is lower than its size would suggest because fully forty percent of the body's volume is empty space.

The surface is a landscape of holes and bridges, where the porous structure is exposed to vacuum. Delicate mineral formations—crystals, threads, and lace-like veils of sublimated minerals—decorate the void spaces, grown over billions of years in the absence of any erosive force. Walking the surface requires careful navigation to avoid thin-crusted areas where the rock could give way into cavities below. The lack of atmosphere means perfect preservation of these fragile structures, a gallery of geological art that would disintegrate at a breath.

The internal cavities range from centimeter-scale pores to chambers large enough to house spacecraft, all connected by a labyrinthine network of passages that penetrates the entire body. This natural architecture has attracted interest from military planners and corporate entities seeking secure, easily defensible installations. The cavities could be sealed, pressurized, and converted to habitable space with relatively modest engineering, creating a naturally hardened facility with walls of solid rock.

A small forward operating base has already been established in one of the larger cavities, used by system patrol vessels as a maintenance and resupply point. The base's inhabitants report that living inside Lace-Fragment creates a unique psychological environment—the awareness that the walls around them are more void than solid, that the entire world is a sponge of rock and emptiness, produces a mild but persistent unease that some find intolerable. Others adapt and come to appreciate the delicate beauty of the mineral formations visible through every viewport, crystalline lacework that has been growing in the dark since before life existed anywhere in the system.
